title: What the Relationship Engine is
description: The engine stores knowledge as a typed graph: nodes are facts, programs, theories, designs, datasets, and disciplines; edges are typed relationships like supports, implements, refutes, or derives-from. Queries traverse the graph to answer relational questions no single document can answer, such as which datasets underpin a theory across disciplines.

architecture: A property-graph store with a fixed relationship vocabulary; typed edge ingestion with evidence requirements; traversal query engine with path constraints.

title: Typed relationship data model
description: Every relationship is a record: source node, target node, relationship type from the controlled vocabulary, evidence pointers, strength score, and timestamps. The vocabulary distinguishes supports from implements from merely mentions, because those differences change what a traversal means.

title: Relationship extraction algorithm
description: Edges are mined from text, code, and metadata: citation parsers find supports edges, import graphs yield uses edges, and experiment sections yield tests edges. Every extracted edge carries its extraction evidence and a confidence score; low-confidence edges are queued for human confirmation instead of entering the graph silently.

title: Multi-hop traversal algorithm
description: The engine's signature move is the multi-hop query: theory to supporting datasets to the programs that processed them to the designs they informed. Traversal respects edge types — a refutes edge flips the meaning of a path — and ranks paths by combined strength so the strongest evidence chains surface first.

demo.title: Runnable code demo — Multi-hop traversal algorithm

architecture: Breadth-first traversal with type-aware path semantics; path strength as product of edge strengths; top-k path ranking; cycle protection.

title: Reasoning: contradiction and support analysis
description: The engine weighs evidence: for any claim it lists supporting and refuting paths, combines strengths, and reports a verdict with the margin. title: Scaling: partitioning the knowledge graph
description: A planetary relationship graph does not fit on one machine. The engine partitions by discipline with cross-partition edge caches, so traversals that stay within a discipline are local and cross-discipline bridges use cached edges. Partitioning is by topic affinity, rebalanced as the graph grows.
